title: Adaptive credit anchors and usage-triggered upgrade prompts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current time-limited trial credit model treats all users the same. We suspect conversion is lower for users whose early activity exceeds the initial credit allocation, and that static expiry windows cause rushed, low-quality evaluation. Goal: Run an experiment that tests two orthogonal levers — adaptive credit 'anchors' (small top-ups tied to milestone events) and contextual, usage-triggered upgrade CTAs — to increase trial-to-paid conversion while controlling unit cost. This ticket scopes the experiment design, rollout plan, metrics, operational requirements, and the gating needed for enterprise customers who require security questionnaire (SQ) reviews before trial unlocks.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment spec documented and approved by Growth and Legal
Instrumentation added: per-user credit event logging, CTA impressions/clicks, conversion attribution within 30 days
Two experimental arms + control implemented in staging and smoke-tested
Data pipeline validates sample size and quality before rollout
Security gating flow for enterprise trial applicants documented and routed to Security/Legal for review
experiment_design: Control: current 30-day / fixed X credits, single passive 'Upgrade' banner in console
Arm A (Anchors): add up to 2 milestone top-ups (anchor credits) when users hit defined events (e.g., 10k tokens used or 5 inference-heavy sessions). Top-ups are modest and time-limited (7 days).

Arm B (Usage-triggered CTAs): keep base credits but surface contextual CTAs—in-product modal with personalized value messaging and one-click upgrade path—triggered when user activity indicates high propensity to convert (high token velocity or integration of API key).
Arm C (Combined): both anchors + contextual CTAs to test additive effects.
Randomization: user-level random assignment at signup with stratification by account type (individual vs org) and region.
Duration & sample: 6-week experiment targeting minimum detectable effect of 8% relative uplift in trial-to-paid conversion with 80% power (approx sample size calculated in analytics doc).
metrics: Primary: trial->paid conversion rate within 30 days
Secondary: time-to-first-paid, ARPU for first 90 days, retention (30/60/90d), NPS for trial cohort
Cost metrics: incremental tokens consumed per converted user, cost-per-conversion, ROI threshold compared to baseline
Safety metrics: incidence of abuse/fraud signals (spike in single-key high-volume usage), customer support contacts related to credits
rollout_plan: Week 0: finalize spec, legal review for messaging and enterprise SQ gating
Week 1: engineering implements experiment flags, credit top-up service hooks, and CTA placements; analytics adds instrumentation
Week 2: QA & staging run; smoke tests with test accounts; update runbooks for customer support
Week 3-8: gradual rollout to randomized cohorts; weekly monitoring dashboard; pause conditions documented
Week 9: analysis and decision: accept variant(s), iterate, roll into default, or run follow-up experiments
risks: Cost overrun if anchors are too generous or abused — mitigation: cap total top-ups per account and add fraud heuristics
Negative UX if CTAs are too aggressive — mitigation: use conservative frequency caps and A/B test messaging tone
Enterprise customers may expect trial without SQ delays — mitigation: surface clear enterprise trial path and provide expedited SQ for named accounts
Data attribution ambiguity for multi-device users — mitigation: require login-backed tracking and mark ambiguous conversions as such in analysis
